items.title: Section: Continuity Begins — Three Ways Seed and Manifestation Keep Each Other's Continuity Alive

items.zh: 復次，云何流轉？謂諸行因果相續不斷性，是謂流轉。又此流轉差別多種。或有種子流轉，謂有種子不現前諸法。或有自在勢力流轉，謂被損種子現行諸法。或有種果流轉，謂有種子，種不被損現行諸法。
items.en:
Seventh, continuity; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is continuity? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. The unbroken succession of cause and effect among conditioned phenomena is called continuity.
Second, distinguishing its kinds; first, briefly stating them. This continuity is furthermore of many distinct kinds. Second, listing and explaining them; first, distinguished by seed and manifestation; first, seed-continuity. There is seed-continuity: phenomena possessing a seed not yet manifesting.
Second, mastery-continuity. There is mastery-continuity: phenomena manifesting while their seed has been suppressed.
Third, seed-and-fruit continuity. There is seed-and-fruit continuity: phenomena possessing a seed, unimpaired, that manifests in activity.

items.title: Section: Continuity Viewed Through Mind and Body, and Through All Three Realms at Once

items.zh: 或有名流流轉，謂四非色蘊。或有色流流轉，謂諸內外十有色處及與法處所攝諸色。又有欲界流流轉，謂欲纏諸行。又有色界流流轉，謂色纏諸行，又有無色流流轉，謂無色纏諸行。
items.en:
Second, distinguished by name and form; first, name-stream continuity. There is name-stream continuity: the four formless aggregates. Second, form-stream continuity. There is form-stream continuity: the ten internal and external material sense-bases, together with form subsumed under the sense-base of mental objects.
Third, distinguished by the three realms; first, desire-realm-stream continuity. There is desire-realm-stream continuity: conditioned phenomena bound by the fetters of the desire realm. Second, form-realm-stream continuity. There is form-realm-stream continuity: conditioned phenomena bound by the fetters of the form realm. Third, formless-realm-stream continuity. There is formless-realm-stream continuity: conditioned phenomena bound by the fetters of the formless realm.

items.title: Section: Continuity Completes — By Feeling, By Moral Quality, and by Whether It Flows With Bondage or Against It

items.zh: 又有樂流流轉，謂樂受及彼所依處。如是苦流流轉、不苦不樂流流轉，當知亦爾。又有善流流轉，謂諸善行。又有不善流流轉，謂諸不善行。又有無記流流轉，謂諸無記行。又有順流流轉，謂順緣起。又有逆流流轉，謂逆緣起。
items.en:
Fourth, distinguished by the three feelings; first, pleasant-stream continuity. There is pleasant-stream continuity: pleasant feeling together with what it depends on. Second, extending this to painful and neutral streams. Painful-stream continuity and neither-pleasant-nor-painful-stream continuity should be understood in just the same way.
Fifth, distinguished by the three moral natures; first, wholesome-stream continuity. There is wholesome-stream continuity: wholesome conduct. Second, unwholesome-stream continuity. There is unwholesome-stream continuity: unwholesome conduct. Third, neutral-stream continuity. There is neutral-stream continuity: neutral conduct.
Sixth, distinguished by forward and reverse dependent origination; first, forward-flowing continuity. There is forward-flowing continuity: following dependent origination. Second, reverse-flowing continuity. There is reverse-flowing continuity: running counter to dependent origination.

items.title: Section: Determinate Distinction — Why Cause and Effect Never Blur, With or Without a Buddha in the World

items.zh: 復次，云何定異？謂無始時來種種因果決定差別無雜亂性，如來出世、若不出世，諸法法爾。又此
items.en: Eighth, determinate distinction; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is determinate distinction? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. From beginningless time, the manifold distinctions among causes and effects remain fixed and free of confusion — this is simply so, whether a tathāgata appears in the world or not.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Determinate Distinction — From Saṃsāra Versus Liberation Down to a Continent's Own Fixed Shape

items.zh: 定異差別多種。或有流轉、還滅定異，謂順逆緣起。或有一切法定異，謂一切法十二處攝，無過無增。或有領受定異，謂一切受三受所攝，無過無增。或有住定異，謂一切內分乃至壽量，一切外分經大劫住。或有形量定異，謂諸有情於彼彼有色生處，所受生身、形量決定，及諸外分四大洲等形量決定。
items.en:
Second, listing and explaining; first, determinate distinction between saṃsāric flow and liberating cessation. There is determinate distinction between saṃsāric flow and liberating cessation: following or running counter to dependent origination.
Second, determinate distinction of all phenomena. There is determinate distinction of all phenomena: all phenomena are subsumed under the twelve sense-bases, neither fewer nor more.
Third, determinate distinction of feeling. There is determinate distinction of feeling: all feeling is subsumed under the three kinds of feeling, neither fewer nor more.
Fourth, determinate distinction of duration. There is determinate distinction of duration: each being's own inner span continues up to its allotted lifespan, while the external world continues for the span of a great eon.
Fifth, determinate distinction of bodily size. There is determinate distinction of bodily size: beings reborn with form in this or that place have a determinate bodily size, just as the four great continents and the rest have a determinate size.

items.title: Section: Correspondence and Its Four Principles — Dependence, Function, Proof, and the Simple Nature of Things

items.zh: 復次，云何相應？謂彼彼諸法為等言說、為等建立、為等開解諸勝方便，是謂相應。又此相應差別分別有四道理。謂觀待道理、作用道理、因成道理、法爾道理。
items.en:
Ninth, correspondence; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is correspondence? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. This or that phenomenon achieves equal statement, equal establishment, and equal, skilful explanation of the most excellent methods — this is called correspondence.
Second, distinguishing its kinds; first, stating it. This correspondence, distinguished further, involves four principles. Second, listing them. Namely, the principle of dependence, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of the simple nature of things.

items.title: Section: Nine Kinds of Speed — From a Galloping Horse to the Single Instant an Ordinary Being Becomes a Noble One

items.zh: 地等已廣分別。復次，云何勢速？謂諸行生滅相應速運轉性，是謂勢速。又此勢速差別多種。或有諸行流轉勢速，謂諸行生滅性。或有地行有情輕健勢速，謂人、象、馬等。或有空行有情勢速，謂諸飛禽、空行藥叉及諸天等。或有言音勢速，謂詞韻捷利。或有流潤勢速，謂江河等迅速流注。或有燒然勢速，謂火焚燎，猛焰飈轉。或有引發勢速，謂放箭、轉丸等。或有智慧勢速，謂修觀者簡擇所知迅速慧性。或有神通勢速，謂大神通者所有運身意勢等速疾神通。
items.en:
Second, the speed of ground-dwelling beings. There is the swift, vigorous speed of ground-dwelling beings: humans, elephants, horses, and the like. Third, the speed of sky-dwelling beings. There is the speed of sky-dwelling beings: birds, sky-travelling spirits, and celestial beings. Fourth, the speed of speech and sound. There is the speed of speech and sound: swift and sharp verbal cadence.
Fifth, the speed of flowing moisture. There is the speed of flowing moisture: rivers and streams rushing swiftly along. Sixth, the speed of burning fire. There is the speed of burning fire: flame burning fiercely, wind-driven. Seventh, the speed of triggered motion. There is the speed of triggered motion: an arrow loosed, a top set spinning, and the like.
Eighth, the speed of wisdom. There is the speed of wisdom: the swift discerning nature of one who practises insight, examining the object of knowledge. Ninth, the speed of supernormal ability. There is the speed of supernormal ability: the swift manifestation of body and mind through the supernormal ability of one of great spiritual power.

items.title: Section: Sequence Begins — Forward Into Bondage Through the Twelve Links, and Backward Into Freedom

items.zh: 復次，云何次第？謂於各別行相續中，前後次第一一隨轉，是謂次第。又此次第差別多種。或有流轉次第，謂無明緣行，廣說乃至生緣老死。或有還滅次第，謂無明滅故行滅，乃至生滅故老死滅。
items.en:
Eleventh, sequence; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is sequence? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. Within each individual continuity of conditioned phenomena, an unbroken order in which each follows the one before — this is called sequence.
Second, distinguishing its kinds; first, briefly stating them. This sequence, distinguished further, is of many kinds. Second, listing and explaining them; first, saṃsāric sequence. There is saṃsāric sequence: ignorance conditions volitional formations, and so on in full, up through birth conditioning ageing and death.
Second, sequence of cessation. There is sequence of cessation: with the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease, and so on, up through the cessation of birth bringing the cessation of ageing and death.

items.title: Section: A Day in Two Lives — the Householder's Routine, and the Monastic's Sequence of Alms, Practice, and Communal Harmony

items.zh: 或有在家、出家行住次第。謂陵旦而起，澡飾其身，被帶衣服，修營事業，調暢沐浴，塗飾香鬘，習近食飲，方乃寢息，是在家者行住次第。若整衣服，為乞食故入聚落等巡次而行，受如法食，還出安坐，食訖澡手，盪鉢，洗足，入空閑室讀誦經典，如理思惟。晝則宴坐、經行，淨修其心，斷滅諸障；至夜中分，少當寢息；於夜後分，速復還起，整服治身，歸所習業。是出家者行住次第。或入僧中，隨其長幼修和敬業，敷設床座，次第受籌，分其臥具、處所、利養及營事業。
items.en:
Third, the sequence of activity for householders and monastics; first, stating it. There is a sequence of activity and repose for householders and for monastics. Second, explaining each; first, householders. Rising at dawn, bathing and grooming the body, dressing and adorning oneself, attending to one's occupation, bathing and relaxing the body, applying scent and floral ornament, gathering to eat and drink, and only then retiring to rest — this is the householder's sequence of activity and repose.
Second, monastics; first, regarding their tasks. Arranging one's robes properly, entering the village in due order to beg for alms, receiving food offered in accordance with the dharma, returning to sit, eating it, washing the hands afterwards, rinsing the bowl, washing the feet, entering a quiet place to recite and reflect on the scriptures. By day, sitting in meditation and walking in mindful pacing, purifying the mind and eliminating obstructions; through the middle of the night, resting briefly; in the final watch, rising again swiftly, arranging robes and body, and returning to one's practice. This is the monastic's sequence of activity and repose.
Second, regarding communal life. Entering the community according to seniority, practising the reverent, harmonious observances, arranging seating, receiving the counting-sticks in due order, and sharing bedding, lodging, material support, and communal duties.

blocks.text: Abstract categories, with a surprisingly concrete ending: the daily routine of a monastic.
The unbroken continuity of cause and effect among conditioned things. Master Cháng Bǎi: seed and manifestation can be cause and effect for each other.

"Name" is the four formless aggregates; "form" is the ten material sense-bases and form included in mental objects. Master Cháng Bǎi: formless beings have no manifest form, but the seeds of form remain.
Forward flow follows dependent origination; reverse flow runs against it. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the three realms all flow forward.

Causes and effects are distinct and unconfused, "whether a tathāgata appears or not". Master Cháng Bǎi: our life is only a flow of karma and result; there is no maker, and it does not arise without cause.
Dependence, function, proof, and the nature of things. Master Cháng Bǎi: proof relies on scripture, direct perception, and inference.
The speed of a fire driven by wind. Master Cháng Bǎi: a little affliction can burn away all one's merit.
From the cessation of ignorance to the cessation of ageing and death. Master Cháng Bǎi: once ignorance is removed, one no longer creates the karma that leads to rebirth.

Seniority is by precept age, not by birth age. Through the middle of the night one rests briefly, and in the last watch rises and returns to practise. Master Cháng Bǎi: the middle watch is roughly nine in the evening to three in the morning.
"A little affliction can burn away all one's merit." Small afflictions are not small: a spark is enough.

quiz.q: What is 流轉, which the English renders "transformation"? Note the risk of confusion with another term.
options: each phenomenon following in unbroken order; the English should be "sequence"
the swift turning of arising and ceasing; the English should be "speed"
fixed, unconfused distinctions of cause and effect; the English "transformation" should instead be "distinction"
the unbroken continuity of cause and effect; the English "transformation" is easily confused with 轉依
quiz.why: The treatise defines 流轉 as the unbroken continuity of cause and effect among conditioned phenomena; Master Cháng Bǎi adds that seed and manifestation may be cause and effect for each other. The English "transformation" stresses change rather than flowing on, and collides with "transformed basis" for 轉依 later in this fascicle.

quiz.q: The English has "phenomena manifesting while their seed has been suppressed." Which two readings does Master Cháng Bǎi list, and which does the English favour?
options: the Commentary: a suppressed seed never manifests; Hán Qīngjìng: the seed is destroyed forever; the English favours the latter
the Commentary: seeds continue by their own kind; Hán Qīngjìng: manifestation infuses seeds; the English keeps both
the Commentary: a suppressed seed still manifests when conditions meet; Hán Qīngjìng: calm suppresses defiled seeds so that good and powers manifest; the English favours the former
the Commentary: the power of Maheśvara; Hán Qīngjìng: the power of the supernormal abilities; the English favours the former
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi lists two readings. The Commentary says a seed, though its force is suppressed, can still manifest when conditions meet. Hán Qīngjìng, like the Sub-commentary, says calm suppresses defiled seeds, so that good and neutral phenomena such as powers manifest with mastery. The English, read plainly, has the suppressed seed's own phenomena manifesting, which fits the former.

quiz.q: What are name-stream transformation and form-stream transformation?
options: name-stream is name, phrase, and syllable; form-stream is the form aggregate
name-stream is feeling and perception; form-stream is the five faculties
name-stream is seeds; form-stream is manifest activity
name-stream is the four formless aggregates; form-stream is the ten material bases with form in the sense-base of mental objects
quiz.why: The treatise says name-stream is the four formless aggregates, and form-stream is the ten internal and external material sense-bases together with form subsumed under the sense-base of mental objects. Master Cháng Bǎi: name means feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness in their unbroken continuity.

quiz.q: Is there form-stream transformation in the formless realm, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: yes as manifestation; no as seeds
not as manifestation; yet as seeds of form, there still is
none at all, the seeds of form being already exhausted there
fully yes, the formless realm having subtle bodies
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the formless realm have no form manifesting, so as to manifestation there is no form-stream transformation; but the seeds of form remain, and in terms of seeds there still is form-stream transformation.

quiz.q: What are forward-flowing and reverse-flowing transformation?
options: wholesome and unwholesome streams
the desire-realm stream and the formless-realm stream in turn
moving towards birth and moving away from ageing
following dependent origination and running counter to it
quiz.why: The treatise says forward-flowing transformation is following dependent origination, and reverse-flowing is running counter to it. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the three realms are all flowing forward, moving along the dependent origination of birth and death.

options: norms set by the Buddha, fading after his passing
fixed, unconfused distinctions among causes and effects, so whether or not a tathāgata appears
long-established customs followed, differing by region
phenomena following in order, without skipping
quiz.why: The treatise defines it as the fixed, unconfused distinctions among causes and effects from beginningless time, simply so whether a tathāgata appears or not. Master Cháng Bǎi: whether or not a buddha appears, all phenomena are so by nature.

quiz.q: What follows about our life from determinate distinction, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: a maker arranges everything according to cause and effect
with no maker there is also no cause or effect
it is only the flow of karma and result, with no maker, and yet not without cause
all is already fixed, and practice cannot change it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the form our life takes is only a flow of karma and result; there is no maker fashioning it, and it does not come about without cause.

quiz.q: What does determinate distinction of feeling state?
options: all feeling is subsumed under the three kinds, neither fewer nor more
all feeling is subsumed under five kinds, neither fewer nor more
all phenomena are subsumed under the twelve bases, neither fewer nor more
each being's inner span continues to its allotted lifespan
quiz.why: The treatise says all feeling is subsumed under the three kinds of feeling, neither fewer nor more. Master Cháng Bǎi: these three contain all feeling and it will neither exceed nor increase. The twelve-base statement belongs to all phenomena, and the lifespan statement to duration.

quiz.q: Among the four principles, how does Master Cháng Bǎi say the principle of proof establishes all phenomena?
options: relying only on customs commonly accepted in the world
relying only on the nature of things, with no need to inquire
relying on scriptural authority, observing by direct perception, and reasoning by inference
relying only on dependence upon verbal designations
quiz.why: The treatise lists the principles of dependence, function, proof, and the simple nature of things. Master Cháng Bǎi on proof: relying on scriptural authority, observing by direct perception, and reasoning by inference, one proves all these phenomena.

quiz.q: The English renders 等 in 為等言說 and the rest as "equal." What two accounts of 等 does the lecture give?
options: Master Cháng Bǎi takes it as "and so on"; the Sub-commentary as waiting
Master Cháng Bǎi takes it as fitting and matching; the Sub-commentary takes it as extending to everything, all being excellent means of good teaching
Master Cháng Bǎi takes it as sameness; the Sub-commentary as immediate succession
both take it as equal in number, so "equal" fits perfectly
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi first explains: names fit what they describe, and causes match their results. Then, with the Sub-commentary, he explains that the Buddhadharma records all phenomena correctly, which is called 等言說. The English "equal" fits only the first account, and it attaches "excellent methods" to the third item alone, though all three belong to it.

quiz.q: What warning does Master Cháng Bǎi draw from the speed of burning fire?
options: a little good can burn away all one's afflictions
fire offerings quickly remove karma
a little affliction can burn away all one's merit
speech wounds faster than fire
quiz.why: The treatise describes flame burning fiercely, driven by wind, as the speed of burning fire. Master Cháng Bǎi draws a warning from it: a little affliction can burn away all one's merit.

quiz.q: The English says "receiving one's portion by lot" for 次第受籌. What is off, and how is seniority counted?
options: 籌 are lots to draw; seniority follows ordination, so the English "by lot" stands
籌 are counting sticks, not lots; seniority follows the order of ordination, not age
籌 are counting sticks; seniority follows age
籌 are community tokens of money; seniority follows birth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the one who received the precepts first is senior and the one later junior; the order is not by age. 籌 in the lecture are wooden sticks for counting people, so "by lot" is inexact, and the English overview itself mentions counting sticks in the same section.

quiz.q: What is the sequence of cessation?
options: with ageing and death ceasing birth ceases, up through formations ceasing and ignorance ceasing
with ignorance ceasing formations cease, up through birth ceasing and ageing and death ceasing
ignorance conditions formations, up through birth conditioning ageing and death
all twelve links cease at once, with no before or after
quiz.why: The treatise gives the order from the cessation of ignorance through the cessation of ageing and death; the conditioning order is saṃsāric sequence. Master Cháng Bǎi: once ignorance is removed, one no longer creates the karma that brings results in the three realms.

quiz.q: How do monastics spend the night, according to the treatise?
options: never lying down, sitting through the whole night
resting briefly through the middle of the night, rising swiftly in the final watch
retiring in the first watch and rising at dawn
walking in the middle of the night and resting in the final watch
quiz.why: The treatise says that through the middle of the night one rests briefly, and in the final watch one rises swiftly and returns to one's practice. Master Cháng Bǎi glosses the middle watch as nine in the evening to three the next morning, a little rest.
